findings.claim: The resolver does not evaluate the member input required by the acceptance criterion, so an arbitrary nonempty member ID can resolve against any case-selected plan key.
findings.evidence: The acceptance criterion says member, plan, procedure, date, and delegation inputs are evaluated. Lines 203-208 only reject a NULL member_id; the candidate queries at lines 209-256 filter on practice, payer, plan_key, service date, and procedure but never use member_id or an enrollment/member-plan relationship. The retained lifecycle test even changes member_id and then successfully resolves the same path, demonstrating that member identity has no effect beyond revision invalidation.
findings.suggested_fix: Resolve or verify the payer-plan enrollment from the member under the verified practice boundary, and use that authoritative membership in candidate selection. Add an integration case where two synthetic members with otherwise identical case inputs map to different plans/entities, plus a refusal for a member that is not enrolled in the selected plan.

findings.claim: Committed resolved outcomes remain valid after their controlling plan, delegation rule, source, or entity changes, allowing downstream work to proceed on obsolete configuration.
findings.evidence: The only invalidation function at lines 52-73 is a trigger on aso.cases and deletes a resolution only when case_input_revision changes. There is no invalidation trigger on aso.payer_plans, aso.plan_delegation_rules, or aso.administering_entities. The read path at lines 84-123 returns the stored resolution without checking matched_rule_id against the rule revision or current entity state. The web gate treats any ready resolved row as sufficient to open downstream evidence, so a rule/path edit or entity deactivation leaves a stale resolved row usable.
findings.suggested_fix: Bind each resolution to immutable/versioned plan, rule, entity, and source versions and reject it on read when any controlling version no longer matches, or atomically invalidate every affected case when configuration changes. Exercise a local integration test that resolves a case, changes each controlling input class, and proves the read becomes unresolved and downstream access stays blocked.

findings.claim: The resolver labels future-effective rules and rules attached to an inactive entity as expired even though neither condition means the rule expired.
findings.evidence: candidate_count excludes rules outside the service-date window and excludes inactive entities at lines 209-224. historical_count at lines 225-232 ignores both effective dates and entity activity. Lines 257-260 classify every candidate_count = 0 / historical_count > 0 result as expired. A rule whose valid_from is after the service date, or a currently effective rule whose entity is inactive, therefore produces the UI statement 'Matching rule expired.'
findings.suggested_fix: Compute expiration from an applicable rule/plan whose end date is on or before the service date. Give future-effective and inactive-entity conditions their own named blocker or map them to an accurate existing configuration state, and add focused fixtures for both cases.

findings.claim: The mounted panel does not present a human-identifiable administering entity or the source behind the selected rule.
findings.evidence: The schema stores administering_entities.name and the resolution carries sourceDocumentId, but ResolutionDetails renders entityId directly as 'Administering entity' at line 121 and renders no source document field at lines 121-126. The central resolved outcome is therefore a UUID with no visible provenance, so an operator cannot verify which organization or policy source controls the path from this panel.
findings.suggested_fix: Return a stable entity key plus display name and reviewable source-document metadata from the authoritative read model, then render those values in the panel while retaining the IDs for internal identity.
